verdicts.summary: Overflow handling and the producer/close ordering hold. The gap is that the thread live buffer is charged for the whole catch-up replay and snapshot phase, while nothing drains it. A busy healthy subscriber can overflow there and get a spurious stream error.
verdicts.location: apps/server/src/ws.ts:1627-1651 (catch-up not drained through deliver); producer at ws.ts:1588-1595
verdicts.scenario: Thread subscription under heavy live traffic while the catch-up replay is slow: the producer started at ws.ts:1588 retains every live event into the output queue via offerAll, but the replay at ws.ts:1627-1642 is concatenated ahead of liveBuffer.stream (ws.ts:1651) and never goes through deliver, so nothing is released until the replay ends. If more than 1000 items (or 8 MiB) accumulate in that window, retain fails at LiveStreamBudget.ts:87, close() clears output, and the first pull after replay fails at LiveStreamBudget.ts:134. The same applies to the snapshot path at ws.ts:1658-1698.
verdicts.consequence: Spurious OrchestrationGetSnapshotError and reconnect for a healthy-but-catching-up subscriber. Converges via cursor resume.
verdicts.missing: Replay throughput and live event rate under load, which are runtime properties and not in the checkout.

verdicts.summary: The shell side has the same gap. The live producer starts before the catch-up replay, and the replay (ws.ts:1522-1537) is not wrapped in deliver. Live events from all threads are charged against the 1000-item cap during the replay. The 'harmless close race' part of the note checks out.
verdicts.location: apps/server/src/ws.ts:1434-1448 (producer, startImmediately) and ws.ts:1522-1537 (unbudgeted catch-up) ahead of synchronizedThenLive at ws.ts:1477-1491
verdicts.scenario: Shell resume with afterSequence where the gap is up to SHELL_RESUME_MAX_GAP (1000, ws.ts:334). The replay is streamed at the client's pace while other threads' domain events keep arriving through the producer at ws.ts:1435-1441, which retains each one. Once more than 1000 items or 8 MiB are buffered, overflow fires and the error surfaces when synchronizedThenLive is first pulled (LiveStreamBudget.ts:134), after the replay finishes.
verdicts.consequence: Spurious shell stream error and reconnect. Converges via afterSequence.
verdicts.missing: Event rate and replay throughput at runtime.

verdicts.summary: Tried the window-vs-offerAll, window-vs-close, and window-overflow orderings. Every path revalidates generation under the mutex, and the failing window fiber releases its permit. No deadlock or double flush.
verdicts.scenario: (a) Window gen 5 has fired and is blocked on mutex.withPermits while offerAll holds the permit and gets a non-update event. offerAll calls cancelWindow (interrupts the waiting fiber, :188 then :116-123) and bumps windowGeneration (:189) before flushPending. If the window reacquires, the generation check at :145 fails and it does nothing. (b) close() runs while a window is pending. It bumps the generation (:212) and cancels the window (:213) under the same mutex. (c) Overflow inside flushPending in flushWindow: replace fails, :155 catchTags absorbs it, :148-154 clears windowFiber, and the forked close at :226-229 waits for the mutex, which is released when the failing fiber returns.

verdicts.summary: Thread live buffer charges the raw activity event before projection, so a large raw completed-tool payload that projects to a tiny summary still overflows the live stream.
verdicts.scenario: A tool.completed (kind tool.completed, persisted with full data at ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:879-897, no cap in this path) with a raw JSON over 8 MiB is appended on a thread with a live subscriber. retain at ThreadLiveEventCoalescer.ts:170 charges the raw bytes because no payload override is passed, and LiveStreamBudget.ts:87 fails before projection. projectActivityEvent (ActivityPayloadProjection.ts:589-600, projectRawOutput at :296-330) would have reduced it to a short summary. The stream errors, and the client reconnects with its cursor, so the replay (unbudgeted, ws.ts:1627-1642) delivers the projected event.
verdicts.consequence: One spurious stream error and reconnect per subscriber, then recovery via replay.
verdicts.missing: Whether provider adapters cap tool output before the event is appended. That code is not in the files I read, so reachability of an over-8 MiB raw payload is unconfirmed.
